question_type: 3-year centered moving average of a derived ratio (duties / value of dutiable imports) assembled from several issues, with a qualifier ('goods subject to duty') narrower than the table's printed total rows; decimal-vs-percent format ambiguity
decisive_step: Mapping the qualifier 'goods subject to duty' onto the table 'Customs Duties and Taxes Collected, and Values of Dutiable and Taxable Imports, Estimated by Tariff Schedules': the 'Free list 3/' block is duty-free goods that only pay Revenue-Act taxes (footnote 3/), so it must be subtracted from BOTH the 'Total duties and taxes' row and the 'Total value of dutiable and taxable imports' row before dividing. The reference made this decision in worklog.md Step 3 (table structure, treasury_bulletin_1941_11.txt:2397-2462, footnote 3/) and encoded it in calc.py (rate = (total duties and taxes - total free list) / (total value - free list value)); vintage assembly (FY1939 from 1941_01, FY1940/41 from 1941_11, calendar-year issues 1941_02-08 skipped) is worklog Step 4 and was NOT the separating step: all three cells got the vintages right. Format: decimal fraction to 3 places (no percent cue in the question), solution.structured.json key_decisions 4.

smallest_change.change: Add to the Alternatives item of AGENTS.md: 'A question's qualifier can be narrower than a table's total row ("goods subject to duty" vs a total "of dutiable and taxable imports"; "marketable" vs "total debt"). When it is, find the component rows the total includes that the qualifier excludes (footnotes tell you: "duty-free", "nonmarketable", "taxed under..."), subtract them from every operand (numerator and denominator), and compute BOTH candidates with calc; answer the one that honours every word of the question. Do not assume the question merely paraphrased the total row.' Plus one line in Percent-or-fraction: 'A "rate" or "ratio" with no percent cue in the question is a decimal fraction.'
would_have_fixed: a (interpretation; a also needed the decimal-format line)
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: it only triggers when a footnoted component sits inside a total the question narrows; the requirement to compute both candidates and choose by wording keeps the total-row reading available when the qualifier matches the total.

alternatives.change: Submit-time rule 'total_vs_qualifier': when a calc input is a cell on a row whose label starts with 'Total' and the same table part contains a component row whose label carries a footnote marker (e.g. 'Free list 3/'), and the question contains a restricting qualifier phrase not in the total's label ('subject to', 'only', 'excluding', 'marketable'), emit: 'Your answer uses row "Total duties and taxes" and "Total value of dutiable and taxable imports"; this table has a footnoted component "Free list 3/" (3/: Duty-free commodities taxed under the Revenue Act of 1932...). The question says "subject to duty". Offer: <your calc with that component subtracted from each operand>.' with Accept/Keep.
alternatives.why_not_first: Costlier to build (needs footnote parsing and operand-to-row binding for both numerator and denominator) and the offer must recompute a two-operand formula; the v8 arms rationalised even after computing the right variant, so an offer might also be 'kept'. Best second step if the text sentence does not move the needle.

alternatives.change: show_table: print footnote text inline after any row label that carries a footnote marker, e.g. the row line becomes '  Free list 3/  [3/ Duty-free commodities taxed under the Revenue Act of 1932 and subsequent acts]', and under NOTES add the composition of each 'Total' row that passes the identity check: 'Total duties and taxes = 16 schedule rows + Miscellaneous 2/ + Total free list (IDENTITY OK)'.
alternatives.why_not_first: All three cells already had the footnote text on screen (a[33], b[38], c[20]) and still chose the total; making it more visible helps the model that never reads footnotes, not the one that reads and rationalises. Still cheap and worth doing for other questions.
